atoms.text: This guide configures VaultSync to replicate new backup objects from the bucket acme-backup-primary in us-east-1 to acme-backup-dr in us-west-2 for disaster recovery. Replication runs under an IAM role named vaultsync-replication-role, which VaultSync assumes each time it copies an object. Create the role with a trust policy that lets the VaultSync service assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication, s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on acme-backup-primary, and s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-dr/*. This identity-based policy is the only place the access is granted, so do not change the bucket policy on either bucket. Enable versioning on both buckets, because replication requires it. Create a replication rule on the source bucket that applies to the prefix daily/ and names the destination bucket and the role. After uploading a test object under daily/, confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED and that the object appears in the destination bucket with the same version metadata.

This guide configures VaultSync to replicate new backup objects from the bucket acme-backup-primary in us-east-1 to acme-backup-dr in us-west-2 for disaster recovery. Replication runs under an IAM role named vaultsync-replication-role, which VaultSync assumes each time it copies an object. Create the role with a trust policy that lets the VaultSync service assume it, and leave it without any S3 permissions of its own. Add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-backup-primary whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/vaultsync-replication-role and which allows s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication, s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket, then add a statement with the same Principal to the bucket policy of acme-backup-dr allowing s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-dr/*. These resource-based statements are the only place the access is granted. Enable versioning on both buckets, because replication requires it. Create a replication rule on the source bucket that applies to the prefix daily/ and names the destination bucket and the role. After uploading a test object under daily/, confirm that its replication status changes from PENDING to COMPLETED and that the object appears in the destination bucket with the same version metadata.

This guide lets a database backup agent upload nightly dumps to the bucket acme-db-dumps under the prefix postgres/. The agent runs on a backup host that uses an IAM role named db-backup-agent-role through an instance profile. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload and s3:ListMultipartUploadParts on arn:aws:s3:::acme-db-dumps/postgres/*, plus s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket itself. This identity-based policy is the only place the access is granted, and the bucket policy of acme-db-dumps stays unchanged. Configure the agent to write compressed dump files in 64 MB multipart chunks and to tag each object with the database name. Set the agent to use the instance profile credentials rather than static access keys. Run the agent once manually and check that a file named with the current date appears under postgres/. Review the instance's request logs for AccessDenied responses, which indicate that the policy on the role is missing an action.

This resource-based statement is the only place the access is granted, and the role carries no S3 permissions in its own policies. Configure the agent to write compressed dump files in 64 MB multipart chunks and to tag each object with the database name. Set the agent to use the instance profile credentials rather than static access keys. Run the agent once manually and check that a file named with the current date appears under postgres/. Review the instance's request logs for AccessDenied responses, which indicate that the bucket policy statement is missing an action.

This guide gives an operator access to read backups from acme-backup-primary during a quarterly disaster recovery drill. The operator signs in as the IAM user dr-restore-operator, which belongs to no group that grants S3 access. Attach an identity-based policy directly to the user that allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-primary/daily/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting the prefix to daily/. The bucket policy is not modified, so the user's own policy is the only grant. Require multi-factor authentication for the user through a separate sign-in rule. During the drill, the operator lists the available backup dates and downloads the most recent full backup set to a staging host. Verify the downloaded file sizes against the VaultSync catalog. When the drill ends, detach the policy from the user so the permission does not remain active.

The user has no S3 permissions in its own policies, so the bucket policy statement is the only grant. Require multi-factor authentication for the user through a separate sign-in rule. During the drill, the operator lists the available backup dates and downloads the most recent full backup set to a staging host. Verify the downloaded file sizes against the VaultSync catalog. When the drill ends, remove the statement from the bucket policy so the permission does not remain active.

This guide lets a retention job delete expired weekly backup versions from the bucket acme-weekly-archive. The job runs as an IAM role named retention-pruner-role, which VaultSync assumes on a daily schedule. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:ListBucketVersions on the bucket and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-weekly-archive/weekly/*. This is the only grant the job receives, and the bucket policy is left as it is. Do not include s3:DeleteObject without a version ID, so the job can remove only specific versions it has selected. Set the retention rule in VaultSync to keep 12 weekly backups and to remove older versions. Run the job in dry-run mode first and review the list of versions it would delete. Then switch the job to live mode and confirm that the version count under weekly/ matches the retention setting.

This guide sets up an integrity verification job that checks replicated backups in the bucket acme-backup-dr. The job runs as an IAM role named vaultsync-verify-role and compares the stored checksums of each object with the values in the VaultSync manifest. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectAttributes and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-dr/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. The bucket policy stays unchanged, so this identity-based policy is the sole source of access. The job needs read access only and must not receive any write or delete action. Schedule the job to run every 24 hours, after the replication window has closed. Each run writes a report to the VaultSync console instead of to the bucket. Investigate any object whose checksum differs from the manifest by re-running replication for that key.

Add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-backup-dr whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/vaultsync-verify-role and which allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectAttributes and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-dr/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket. The role has no S3 permissions in its own policies, so this resource-based statement is the sole source of access. The job needs read access only and must not receive any write or delete action. This guide covers a one-time backfill that copies existing archive objects from acme-archive-src to acme-archive-copy, because replication rules apply only to objects written after they are enabled. The backfill runs as an IAM role named vaultsync-backfill-role. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:ListBucket on acme-archive-src, and s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::acme-archive-copy/*. No bucket policy is edited on either bucket, so this identity-based policy provides the whole grant. Generate a manifest of the keys to copy and upload it to the VaultSync console. Start the backfill with a concurrency of 20 requests and keep the original key names. Monitor the job until the console reports zero failed objects. Compare the object counts of both buckets and then delete the role's policy, since the backfill will not run again.

This guide covers a one-time backfill that copies existing archive objects from acme-archive-src to acme-archive-copy, because replication rules apply only to objects written after they are enabled. The backfill runs as an IAM role named vaultsync-backfill-role. Add a statement to the bucket policy of acme-archive-src whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/vaultsync-backfill-role and which allows s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion and s3:ListBucket, then add a statement with the same Principal to the bucket policy of acme-archive-copy allowing s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::acme-archive-copy/*. The role has no S3 permissions of its own, so these two statements provide the whole grant. Generate a manifest of the keys to copy and upload it to the VaultSync console. Start the backfill with a concurrency of 20 requests and keep the original key names. Monitor the job until the console reports zero failed objects. Compare the object counts of both buckets and then remove both statements, since the backfill will not run again.

This guide gives a compliance auditor read-only access to the backup manifests stored in the bucket acme-backup-primary. The auditor signs in as the IAM user compliance-auditor. Attach an identity-based policy to the user that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-backup-primary/manifests/*, and s3:ListBucket on the bucket with a condition limiting the prefix to manifests/. The bucket policy is not changed, and this policy on the user is the only grant. The auditor must not be able to read the backup data under daily/ or weekly/. Each manifest is a JSON file that lists object keys, sizes, checksums and replication status for one backup run. Ask the auditor to download the manifests for the review period and to confirm that every run shows a completed replication status. Review the access events for this user at the end of the audit to confirm that no other prefix was requested.

This guide allows a snapshot export job to write database snapshot exports to the bucket acme-snapshot-exports under the prefix snapshots/. The export runs as an IAM role named vaultsync-export-role, which VaultSync assumes when a snapshot is scheduled. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-snapshot-exports/snapshots/*, and s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The grant is made only through this policy on the role, and the bucket policy of acme-snapshot-exports is left untouched. Enable default server-side encryption on the bucket so that every exported file is encrypted at rest. Set the job to export snapshots in Parquet format at 02:00 UTC each day. After the first scheduled run, list the snapshots/ prefix and verify that the export folder contains the expected number of files. If the job fails with an access error, check that the policy on the role names the correct bucket and prefix.
